My read: 99.7% regional is below our standard global 99.9% but is plausible with a regional carveout if we cap credits and add cross-region fallback. The sticking point is the 25% credits cap — that's above our typical 10-15% ceiling for critical customers. If we accept 25% we should:

- Require a hard incident definition (we should limit what counts as a valid creditable outage).
- Add an availability remediation plan (two-week rollback / variant fallback + runbook access).
- Limit the credit window to the first 12 months only.

Marissa — can you draft a redline with a defined incident taxonomy, a shift-left requirement (engineering runbooks + contact), and propose a credits cap of 20% with an option to escalate to 25% only with exec sign-off? Put together recommended language so I can loop in Jonas + Sean for exec approval.

Soojin / Jonas —

Draft points (high level) I've prepared for the contract redline (see attached term sheet):

1) Uptime: Carveout clause: Redwood will provide a regional uptime target of 99.70% for the "US-EAST" region for a period of 12 months from start of production. All other standard SLOs remain in effect.

2) Service Credit Cap: Base cap at 20% of monthly recurring fees for any rolling 30-day window. If cumulative credits exceed 20% in any 90-day window, Redwood will engage in an executive review to determine remedial measures. Any cap increase above 20% (to a maximum of 25%) requires explicit written approval by Redwood executive (VP Sales + CFO or COO).

3) Incident Taxonomy: We will enumerate credit-eligible events (regional infra, Redwood runtime failures). Exclusions: customer misconfiguration, third-party provider downtime, planned maintenance with 72-hour notice.

4) Mitigations: Cross-region routing for failover will be available; customer must enable it and accept region-to-region latency trade-offs. Redwood will provide runbooks and a post-incident RCA within 10 business days for incidents >4 hours.

5) Commercial trade: 20% committed usage discount for 12-month prepay, contingent on the above SLO language and the 20% credit cap. Any acceptance of 25% cap requires exec signoff as above.

If Jonas + Sean sign off on exec approval language (we need names), I'll update the commercial-term-sheet-PLT-4789.pdf and we'll send back to Alex with a DocuSign request.

Marissa
